title: GM strategies are not a Nash equilibrium in l-player exact slow NIM(n, n-1) for n, l >= 3: a refutation of Gurvich-Naumova Conjecture 1 (arXiv:2311.03257)
beyond_target: accepted after the campaign target of 40 was reached (additional result #47 toward 60)
exact_endpoint: SlowNim360653.conjecture1_false : ¬ SlowNim360653.Conjecture, where Conjecture := for all n >= 2, l >= 2, initial positions x : Fin n -> N and rational C exceeding the length of every play from x under every legal positional profile, the all-GM profile (minimal multiple of l kept, largest index; largest entry kept when no multiple exists) is a Nash equilibrium for the payoff -(C - L) to the loser (player L mod l) and (C - L)/(l - 1) to each other player against every legal positional unilateral deviation; witnessed at n = l = 3, x = (4,4,5), C = 7
scope: Conjecture 1 fails for every n >= 3 and l >= 3 (ordinary block-invariant proof; Lean certifies (4,4,5)); a computed certificate at (5,5,6) shows no completion of the no-multiple convention rescues it; l = 2 is the GMMV23 theorem

substantive_reason: It refutes a stated equilibrium conjecture for multiplayer exact slow NIM in the source's own game, payoff and GM rule, for every n >= 3 and l >= 3, by a sign-changing unilateral deviation (a loss becomes a win) with exact block-invariant lengths, and shows that the positive l = 2 theorem does not extend. The source analyses only GM trajectories; the deviation analysis is new, not a source-formula evaluation or a printed example.
